summary: Iteration 29 retest of refunds in partially shipped orders. FIXED. Case 1: qty 2, ship 1, then refund 1 (the shipped unit). cancelled_qty stays 0 and stock is unchanged (on_hand 9, reserved 1). The order stays partially_shipped, the remaining unit ships (201), and the vendor order becomes 'shipped'. Both shipments then go to delivered and the vendor order becomes 'delivered'. Case 2: qty 2, ship 1, then refund 2. Exactly 1 unit is cancelled and its hold is released once (reserved 1 -> 0, on_hand stays 9). The vendor order moves partially_shipped -> shipped with a system 'shipped' order_event. Shipping more is rejected, but with 409, not the 422 in the brief (see minor issues). Another refund is rejected and the counts don't change. test_phase15_t1_refund_cancel.py now has 7 tests (2 new: test_06, test_07): 7/7 pass. Regression, each file run separately: prelaunch 6/6, phase07 7/7, phase08 12/12 on the first run (no flakes this time). Final DB: users 1, 0 vendors, stores, products, variants, inventory, orders, order_items, vendor_orders, payments, refunds, shipments, payouts, ledger_entries and commission_ledger. commission_rules 16.

minor.issue: On a vendor order that is already 'shipped' (including one closed by a refund), shipping more returns 409 invalid_transition with the message 'Accept the order before shipping it.' The brief expected 422. The status gate in api/v1/fulfillment.py create_shipment (line ~306) fires before the qty check. A normally fully shipped order gives the same 409, so the behaviour is consistent, but the message is misleading. Suggest a status-specific message, e.g. 'This order has already shipped' or 'This order is cancelled'.
Still carried over from iteration 28: the conditional update has no retry if shipped_qty or cancelled_qty change at the same moment. Rare.

971 older notifications belong to TEST users that no longer exist. They were there before this run and the test suites' teardowns don't remove all of them. T1 removed the 78 created by this run. There is also 1 orphan wishlist (user 6af11fef…), the same one reported in iteration 28.

critical_code_review_comments: _cancel_unshipped: n = min(refunded - shipped - cancelled, quantity - shipped - cancelled). It treats refunds as covering shipped units first, which is correct for damage and returns. Side effect: when an order is partially shipped, a refund that was actually meant as a cancellation of the unshipped unit leaves that unit shippable. That is a business choice; the admin would need to refund all remaining units to cancel it.
_close_if_nothing_left: correctly handles both cases (some units shipped -> 'shipped'; nothing shipped -> 'cancelled'). It is idempotent through conditional find_one_and_update on status.
Delivery of shipped orders only happens through shipment status updates. The vendor order status endpoint returns 409 for 'delivered' on shipped orders, which is intended.
